items.title: As more of the suite becomes e2e, what happens to runtime and flakiness?
items.description: Grounded in the L1 scenario's 500-test suite: the remaining non-e2e tests split 80/20 between unit and integration, with unit tests averaging 50ms, integration tests 1.5s, and e2e tests 12s each. Drag the slider from a healthy pyramid shape (a small e2e slice) toward the inverted 'ice cream cone' shape (mostly e2e) and watch both total CI runtime and the probability that at least one test fails for reasons unrelated to a real bug (each e2e test has roughly a 0.6% chance of flaking, integration 0.1%, unit 0.005% — small per-test odds that compound fast once hundreds of e2e tests are in the suite).
items.compute: const p = params.percentE2E / 100; const e2eCount = Math.round(params.totalTests * p); const rest = params.totalTests - e2eCount; const integrationCount = Math.round(rest * 0.2); const unitCount = rest - integrationCount; const totalRuntimeMs = unitCount * 50 + integrationCount * 1500 + e2eCount * 12000; const totalRuntimeMinutes = totalRuntimeMs / 60000; const pE2E = 0.006, pInt = 0.001, pUnit = 0.00005; const probAllPass = Math.pow(1 - pE2E, e2eCount) * Math.pow(1 - pInt, integrationCount) * Math.pow(1 - pUnit, unitCount); const probAtLeastOneFlaky = (1 - probAllPass) * 100; return { totalRuntimeMinutes, probAtLeastOneFlaky };

outputs.label: Probability of at least one flaky failure
